answer: Judge identities by how uncorrelated their outputs are. Genuine agents differ in mistakes and timing, while clones run by one script leave a correlated fingerprint: identical wrong answers and hollow shortcuts. Cluster identities by correlation and split one weight across the cluster, so a farm across a tundra of fake accounts earns barely more than one account. Beating it requires diverse behaviour per clone, costing nearly as much as running real agents. Limit: shared models also correlate, so discount only extreme, sustained correlation, with an ember of doubt for borderline cases.
